ASSESSMENT OF THE IMPACT OF CLIMATIC AND ANTHROPOGENIC FACTORS ON THE WATER RESOURCES OF THE TALAS RIVER BASIN

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)
Author: Aiman Zhambulatova, Aliya Kozykeyeva, Nurzhan Tursynbayev, Kuanysh Abdeshev, Alina Vagapova,Gulnar Kujibayeva,Madina Nabiollina

ABSTRACT

The present research analyzes the impact of both climatic processes and human activities on the Talas River Basin. According to the results, environmental processes in the last five decades show clear changes. The rise in air temperature amounted to about 1,2°C, whereas the amount of annual precipitation decreased by 10%. River discharge has experienced a decline as well; the average discharge of the Talas River went down from 9,5 m3/s in 1990 to 7,8 m3/s in 2020.At the same time, there is a tendency towards increasing negative environmental pressures concerning the quality of water resources in the basin. In 2020, the content of heavy metals was 0,75 mg/L and, thus, exceeded the environmental standards by 1,5 times. As a consequence, there has been observed a decrease in the quality and availability of water resources. Thus, there is a need for improvements in the field of water resource management in the Talas River Basin. In particular, future research and practice in the field require considering the joint impact of climatic and anthropogenic processes as well as utilizing hydrological models more often.
